Thank you — below is a 12‑week resistance + aerobic training program and nutrition plan tailored for a 45‑year‑old woman with type 2 diabetes (on metformin) whose HbA1c is 7.2%. The program focuses on fat loss and improving glycaemic control, uses a full gym, and includes clear weekly structure, exercises, sets/reps, progression, and diabetes‑specific nutrition and safety guidance. Before starting: confirm medical clearance with her GP (especially if she has cardiovascular disease, neuropathy, retinopathy or other complications), check current medications and symptoms, and review hypoglycaemia awareness and action (metformin rarely causes hypoglycaemia alone, but exercise can change glucose responses).

Key principles
- Combine progressive resistance training (improves insulin sensitivity and preserves lean mass) with both moderate continuous and interval aerobic work (improves glucose control).
- Create a modest energy deficit for fat loss (≈300–500 kcal/day below estimated maintenance) while preserving protein intake and strength work to protect muscle.
- Emphasize carbohydrate timing around workouts and consistent meal patterns to reduce glycaemic variability.
- Monitor blood glucose pre/post exercise in early weeks to learn her individual responses (especially if she uses other glucose‑lowering meds in future).
- Prioritise recovery, sleep, and gradual progression to reduce injury risk.

Baseline assumptions (adjust to client specifics)
- Current fitness: beginner–intermediate gym user.
- No major diabetic complications preventing exercise.
- Bodyweight and maintenance calories unknown — nutrition will give ranges and methods to individualise.
- She is taking metformin only; hypoglycaemia risk is low but possible with large activity or irregular eating.

Safety and monitoring
- Ask her to measure blood glucose before and after the first several sessions (and during longer sessions >60 min) to learn patterns. Typical plan: check pre‑exercise and 30 minutes post‑exercise for first 2 weeks, then as needed.
- If pre‑exercise glucose <5.0 mmol/L (90 mg/dL) consider a small carbohydrate snack (10–20 g carbs) and recheck in 10–15 minutes. If >13.9 mmol/L (250 mg/dL) and ketones present or symptomatic, avoid strenuous exercise until medical advice.
- Stay hydrated, avoid long fasted high‑intensity sessions initially, and carry fast‑acting carbs if concerned.
- Encourage regular contact with prescribing clinician about medication changes if weight loss or activity level changes substantially.

Overall 12‑week structure
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Adaptation — build consistency, teach movement, establish baseline aerobic capacity. 3 resistance sessions + 2 moderate aerobic sessions + 1 optional active recovery/day.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Intensification — increase resistance load, add structured interval cardio, increase NEAT. 3 resistance + 2 cardio (one HIIT) + 1 mobility/balance.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Consolidation and peak fat‑loss push — highest load/volume in resistance, two interval sessions (one shorter high intensity, one longer steady state), refeed considerations and testing. 3 resistance + 2 cardio + 1 restoration.

Weekly schedule template (example)
- Monday: Resistance Session A (full‑body focus)
- Tuesday: Cardio 1 — moderate continuous (30–40 min brisk walk / bike / elliptical)
- Wednesday: Resistance Session B (upper focus + core)
- Thursday: Active recovery / mobility or HIIT depending on phase
- Friday: Resistance Session C (lower focus + posterior chain)
- Saturday: Cardio 2 — interval or longer moderate session
- Sunday: Rest or light activity (walk, yoga)

Progression principle: increase loads by ~2–10% when target reps are achieved with good form; add 1 set or reduce rest to increase intensity; progress cardio intensity or duration gradually.

Detailed week‑by‑week plan

Phase 1 — Weeks 1–4: Adaptation and consistency
Goal: teach technique, establish 3×/week resistance routine, control glycaemia with added activity.

Weeks 1–2
Resistance sessions: 3×/week (M/W/F). Light–moderate intensity, RPE 5–7/10.

Session A — Full body (approx. 45–55 min)
- Warm‑up: 5–8 min brisk walk + dynamic mobility
- Squat variation (goblet or box squat): 3 sets × 10–12 reps
- Push (machine chest press or dumbbell bench): 3 × 10–12
- Row (seated cable or single‑arm dumbbell row): 3 × 10–12 each side
- Romanian deadlift (dumbbell or trap bar, hinge pattern): 3 × 10–12
- Standing dumbbell shoulder press: 2 × 12
- Core: Pallof press or dead bug: 2 × 30–45 sec
- Cool down & light stretching

Session B — Upper emphasis (approx. 40–50 min)
- Warm‑up: 5 min bike + shoulder mobility
- Lat pulldown or assisted pull‑up: 3 × 10–12
- Incline dumbbell press: 3 × 10–12
- Seated cable row: 3 × 10–12
- Lateral raises: 2 × 12–15
- Biceps curl superset triceps pushdown: 2 × 12 each
- Core: Plank: 3 × 20–30 sec

Session C — Lower emphasis (approx. 45–55 min)
- Warm‑up: 5–8 min elliptical + hip mobility
- Leg press or Bulgarian split squat (bodyweight to start): 3 × 10–12 per leg
- Glute bridge or hip thrust (bodyweight to light load): 3 × 12–15
- Hamstring curl (machine): 2 × 12
- Calf raise: 2 × 12–15
- Farmer carry or suitcase carry: 2 × 40–60 m
- Core: Side plank 2 × 20–30 sec each side

Cardio (Tue, Sat)
- Two sessions/week:
  - Session 1 (Tue): 30 min moderate continuous — brisk walk, elliptical or bike at conversational pace (RPE 4–5).
  - Session 2 (Sat): 25–30 min steady state or walking hills; keep intensity moderate.

Recovery:
- Aim for 7–9 hours sleep, 1–2 light mobility sessions; check blood glucose pre/post first sessions to monitor response.

Nutrition (Weeks 1–4)
Calorie target:
- Aim for ~300–500 kcal/day deficit from estimated maintenance. If maintenance unknown, use rough starting suggestion: 1,600–1,800 kcal/day if sedentary and average height, adjust after 2 weeks. Alternatively calculate using Mifflin St Jeor and activity factor.
Macronutrients:
- Protein: 1.2–1.6 g/kg bodyweight/day (to preserve lean mass). Example: if 70 kg, 84–112 g/day.
- Fat: 25–35% of calories (choose unsaturated fats).
- Carbohydrate: remainder of calories; distribute evenly across meals (see timing).
Carbohydrate timing and glycaemic control:
- Spread carbs across 3 meals + 1–2 snacks to avoid large postprandial spikes.
- Aim for 30–45 g carbohydrate per main meal as a starting point; adjust based on glucose monitoring. Prioritise lower‑GI carbs (whole grains, legumes, non‑starchy veg), fibre, and combine carbs with protein and fat.
- Pre‑workout: small snack with ~15–25 g carbs + protein ~30–60 min before moderate sessions if needed (helps performance, reduces hypoglycaemia risk).
- Post‑workout: include ~15–30 g carbs with 20–30 g protein to aid recovery and stabilise glucose.
Micronutrients and hydration:
- Fibre target 25–35 g/day.

Important: confirm medical clearance from her GP before starting. Continue to monitor blood glucose responses (see safety section). If she develops other diabetes medications that increase hypoglycaemia risk (e.g., insulin, sulfonylureas), contact prescribing clinician to revise plan.

SUMMARY: structure at a glance
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4) Adaptation: teach movement, establish routine. 3 resistance sessions/week + 3 fasted morning steady‑state cardio sessions/week + 2 fed cardio/conditioning/light sessions. Weekly cheat meal included (one meal/week). Eating window default: 12:12 TRE (e.g., 07:30–19:30).
- Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8) Intensification: raise resistance loads, introduce fed HIIT intervals, maintain 3 fasted morning cardio sessions/week (low–moderate), adjust nutrition slightly upward around training.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12) High‑intensity push: heavy compounds, cluster and density work, two fed HIIT sessions/week, fasted cardio kept low‑moderate, weekly cheat meal after resistance session. Deload in week 12.

Safety & monitoring (read first)
- Medical clearance required.
- Blood glucose checks: baseline course — check fasting morning glucose daily first week; pre‑exercise and 30–60 min post‑exercise for the first 2 weeks of new intensity or new sessions; thereafter spot‑check as needed.
- Hypoglycaemia protocol: If pre‑exercise glucose <5.0 mmol/L (90 mg/dL) eat 10–20 g carbs then recheck in 10–15 min. If symptomatic or <3.9 mmol/L, treat with 15–20 g fast carbs and seek help if persists.
- Hyperglycaemia caution: If glucose >13.9 mmol/L (250 mg/dL) with symptoms or ketones, avoid intense exercise until medical advice.
- Carry fast‑acting carbs (juice, glucose gel) for early sessions until patterns known.
- Avoid high‑intensity fasted sessions; schedule HIIT fed.
- Monitor sleep, mood, training RPE and resting HR; reduce intensity if recovery poor.
- Check B12 periodically (metformin can reduce B12).

Calorie and macronutrient guidance (baseline)
- Aim for modest deficit: ~300–500 kcal/day below maintenance. If unknown, coach choose starting target (e.g., 1,600 kcal/day as example) and adjust by weight trend.
- Protein: 1.2–1.6 g/kg/day (prefer 1.4–1.6 during Phase 3).
- Fat: 25–35% of calories (focus on unsaturated fats).
- Carbs: remaining calories; distribute across meals and around training. On higher intensity days increase peri‑workout carbs.
- Fibre target 25–35 g/day. Hydrate well.
- TRE default: 12:12 eating window (07:30–19:30). If she wants to trial 16:8, do so cautiously with medical sign‑off and monitoring.

Weekly template (default)
- Monday: AM fasted steady‑state cardio (30–35 min) + Resistance A (PM)
- Tuesday: AM fasted steady‑state cardio (20–30 min) + later HIIT (fed) or mobility depending on phase
- Wednesday: Resistance B (PM)
- Thursday: AM fasted steady‑state cardio (20–30 min) + mobility/light
- Friday: Resistance C (PM) + weekly cheat meal after training (planned)
- Saturday: Cardio 2 (fed intervals / longer tempo) + optional active recovery
- Sunday: Rest or light walk / mobility

Progression rules
- Increase load 2–10% when top reps achieved with good form. For strength sets, add weight when target reps hit. For accessory sets, add reps or reduce rest.
- Monitor recovery; if two consecutive workouts feel substantially harder, reduce load or volume.
- Reassess at 4 and 8 weeks.

Detailed session plans — Weeks 1–12

PHASE 1 — WEEKS 1–4: ADAPTATION
Goals: movement patterns, consistency, low–moderate cardio in morning fasted state, modest caloric deficit.

Notes for phase: fasted AM cardio 3×/week at low–moderate intensity (RPE 3–4; 20–30 min weeks 1–2, 25–35 min weeks 3–4). Resistance sessions later fed. Pre‑fasted cardio check: if glucose <5.0 mmol/L, eat 10–20 g carbs.

Weeks 1–2 (Technique & volume)
Resistance: M/W/F (PM). RPE 5–7.

Session A — Full body (Mon)
- Warm‑up: 5–8 min brisk walk or bike + dynamic mobility
- Goblet squat or box squat: 3 × 10–12 (rest 60–90 sec)
- Dumbbell or machine chest press: 3 × 10–12 (60–90 sec)
- Seated cable row or one‑arm dumbbell row: 3 × 10–12 each (60–90 sec)
- Romanian deadlift (light): 3 × 10–12 (60–90 sec)
- Standing dumbbell shoulder press: 2 × 12 (60 sec)
- Pallof press or dead bug: 2 × 30–45 sec
- Cool down & stretch

Session B — Upper focus (Wed)
- Warm‑up: 5 min bike + shoulder mobility
- Lat pulldown or assisted pull‑up: 3 × 10–12
- Incline dumbbell press: 3 × 10–12
- Seated cable row: 3 × 10–12
- Lateral raises: 2 × 12–15
- Biceps curl superset triceps pushdown: 2 × 12 each
- Plank: 3 × 20–30 sec

Session C — Lower focus (Fri)
- Warm‑up: 5–8 min elliptical + hip mobility
- Leg press or Bulgarian split squat: 3 × 10–12 per leg
- Glute bridge or hip thrust (bodyweight): 3 × 12–15
- Hamstring curl (machine): 2 × 12
- Calf raise: 2 × 12–15
- Farmer carry: 2 × 40–60 m
- Side plank: 2 × 20–30 sec each

Cardio (fasted mornings)
- Mon/Tue/Thu mornings: 20–30 min brisk walk / easy bike / elliptical at RPE 3–4. Hydrate; black coffee ok. Carry fast carbs until patterns known.

Other cardio
- Sat: 25–30 min moderate walk or easy incline walking (fed if preferred)
- Sun: rest/light walking

Nutrition specifics (Phase 1)
- Calories: start modest deficit (e.g., 1,600–1,800 kcal depending on client). Track 3–4 days to adjust.
- Protein: 1.2–1.4 g/kg/day.
- Carbs: 30–45 g per main meal starting guideline; spread across meals. Post cardios: small snack with 15–30 g carbs + 15–25 g protein.
- Cheat meal: Friday dinner (moderate portion). Keep rest of day balanced.

Weeks 3–4 (Progression)
- Resistance: start shifting some sets to 8–10 reps for progression. Increase load if 12 reps comfortable.
- Fasted cardio: increase to 25–35 min, keep intensity low–moderate. Introduce one short tempo in week 4 only if glucose stable: 3 × 2 min slightly harder with 3 min easy.
- Sat cardio: increase to 30–35 min steady or light hills.
- Nutrition: recheck weight and adjust calories down 100–150 kcal if weight not moving and hunger manageable.

PHASE 2 — WEEKS 5–8: INTENSIFICATION
Goals: increase resistance stimulus, introduce fed HIIT once/week, maintain morning fasted steady state cardio 3×/week.

Fast cardio: Mon/Tue/Thu mornings: 25–35 min steady state (RPE 3–5). Always check pre‑session glucose.

Weeks 5–6
Resistance: maintain 3 sessions (M/W/F). Rep ranges become mixed (strength + hypertrophy).

Session A — Strength emphasis (Mon PM)
- Warm‑up
- Back squat (or goblet/trapbar): 4 × 6–8 (90–120 sec)
- Romanian deadlift: 3 × 8–10
- Incline dumbbell press: 3 × 8–10
- Bent over row: 3 × 8–10
- Pallof press: 3 × 30–40 sec

Session B — Upper & conditioning (Wed PM)
- Warm‑up
- Seated cable row: 4 × 8–10
- Dumbbell bench press: 3 × 8–10
- Single‑arm dumbbell shoulder press: 3 × 8–10
- Superset TRX face pulls 3 × 12 + band pull‑aparts 3 × 12
- Farmer carry: 3 × 40–60 m
- 10 min steady bike cooldown

Session C — Lower & posterior (Fri PM)
- Warm‑up
- Deadlift variation (trapbar preferred for comfort): 4 × 5–8
- Walking lunges: 3 × 8–10 per leg
- Hip thrust: 3 × 8–10 (progress load)
- Hamstring curl: 3 × 10–12
- Calf raises: 3 × 12–15

Cardio / HIIT (fed)
- Sat: HIIT introduced (fed): 6–8 × 1 min higher effort (RPE 7–8) with 90–120 sec easy recovery. Total session ~25–30 min incl warm‑up/cool down.

Nutrition adjustments (Phase 2)
- Protein: 1.3–1.5 g/kg/day.
- Peri‑workout carbs: pre‑workout snack 15–30 g carbs when performing HIIT or heavy resistance in fed state; post‑workout 20–30 g carbs + 20 g protein.
- Reassess calories at week 6 and reduce 100–150 kcal if needed.

Weeks 7–8 (Progression)
- Increase loads on main lifts by ~2–5% when progressed. Add a set to main lifts or shorten rest to increase challenge.
- Fasted cardio: two steady sessions + one with light tempo allowed only if glucose stable (e.g., 3 × 2–3 min tempo).
- Sat HIIT: progress to 8–10 intervals or increase intensity (shorter recovery) if tolerated and glucose stable.

PHASE 3 — WEEKS 9–12: HIGH‑INTENSITY PUSH
Goals: push intensity, increase metabolic demand, preserve lean mass. Continue morning fasted cardio low/moderate; schedule HIIT and heavy resistance fed.

Important Phase‑3 diabetes notes
- Continue pre/post glucose checks for first 1–2 weeks of Phase 3. High intensity can transiently raise glucose; monitor and respond.
- Avoid high‑intensity fasted sessions. Have a small pre‑workout snack (15–25 g carbs + small protein) before any morning HIIT if performed.
- Keep fast‑acting carbs at hand.

Weekly layout (Weeks 9–11 are highest load; week 12 is deload/test)
- Mon: AM fasted steady state 30–35 min; PM Resistance A heavy
- Tue: HIIT (fed) — high intensity
- Wed: Resistance B heavy + short finisher
- Thu: Active recovery/mobility + optional light fasted walk
- Fri: Resistance C (power + metabolic circuits) + cheat meal after training
- Sat: HIIT long intervals or metabolic conditioning (fed)
- Sun: Rest/light recovery

Detailed Weeks 9–12

Week 9 (intro to high intensity)
Session A (Mon PM) — Heavy full‑body
- Warm‑up 8–10 min
- Back squat: 5 × 5 @ ~75–80% 1RM (2–3 min)
- Romanian deadlift: 3 × 6–8 (2 min)
- Bench press: 4 × 6–8 (90–120 sec)
- Bent over row/T‑bar: 3 × 6–8
- Pallof press/core: 3 × 10–12
- Finisher (optional): 8 min EMOM — odd: burpees x6 / even: kb swings x12 (scale)

Session B (Tue HIIT — fed)
- Warm‑up 10 min
- 10–12 × 30 sec all‑out on bike/row/sprint with 60–90 sec easy recovery
- Cool down 8–10 min
- Check glucose pre/post

Session C (Wed PM)
- Deadlift: 4 × 4–6 heavy (2–3 min)
- Bulgarian split squat: 3 × 8 per leg
- Overhead press: 4 × 6–8
- Pull‑ups/assisted or lat pulldown: 3 × 6–8
- Superset lateral raise 3 × 12 + face pulls 3 × 15
- 10 min moderate row finish

Session D (Fri PM) — Lower + power + metabolic
- Warm‑up
- Trapbar jumps or low box jumps: 4 × 4–6 (explosive)
- Front/safety squat: 4 × 5–6
- Hip thrust heavy: 4 × 6–8
- Hamstring curl: 3 × 10–12
- Farmer carry heavy: 3 × 40–60 m
- Metabolic circuit: 3 rounds (30 sec effort/15 sec change): mountain climbers / slam ball / sled push — rest 90 sec

Sat (Long intervals/tempo — fed)
- 4 × 4 min at hard pace (RPE 7–8) with 3 min easy recovery OR 30–40 min tempo ride/run (RPE 6–7)

Week 10 (increase density)
- Add cluster sets on squat or deadlift if technique solid: e.g., 5 sets of (3 reps @ 80% with 15–20 sec intra‑set rest).
- Shorten accessory rests to 30–45 sec to increase metabolic demand.
- Add a 4‑minute Tabata finisher after one resistance session (20 sec on / 10 sec off × 8).

Week 11 (peak)
- Increase main lifts intensity to ~80–85% for some sets:
  - Squat example: 6 × 3 @ 80–85% 1RM
  - Deadlift: 5 × 3 @ 80–85%
- HIIT sessions: Tue 12 × 30 sec with 60 sec recovery; Sat 6 × 2 min high with 2 min recovery.
- Include one metabolic AMRAP (20–25 min) as a conditioning test (e.g., 10 kb swings, 8 goblet squats, 6 push‑ups, 200 m row).

Week 12 (deload + testing)
- Reduce volume 30–40% but keep intensity for short sets.
- Example:
  - Back squat: 3 × 3 @ 85% (or a single heavy triple if coaching support)
  - Deadlift: 3 × 3 @ 80–85%
  - Keep HIIT to shorter session: 6 × 30 sec
  - Reduce accessory volume
- Reassess: bodyweight, waist, strength estimate, subjective energy and glucose logs. Prepare maintenance plan after 12 weeks.

Pre/Post‑Workout nutrition (general)
- Fasted AM cardio: plain water, black coffee/tea ok. If pre‑exercise glucose <5.0 mmol/L, have 10–20 g carbs (half banana, 1 rice cake) then recheck.
- Post‑cardio (if fasted): eat within 30–60 min a balanced meal: 20–30 g protein + 20–40 g carbs + veg/fat. Example: omelette + 1 slice whole‑grain toast + berries.
- Resistance/HIIT (fed): pre‑workout snack 60–90 min prior: 20–40 g carbs + 15–25 g protein. Post‑workout 15–30 g carbs + 20–30 g protein within 30–60 min.
- If not hungry after morning cardio but resistance session later, keep protein intake across later meals to meet daily protein target.

Quick post‑workout snack options (portable)
- 150–200 g Greek yogurt + berries
- Protein shake (20–25 g protein) + 1/2 banana
- Cottage cheese + fruit
- Tuna pouch + 2 crispbreads

Fasted cardio specifics (integrated)
- Frequency: Mon/Tue/Thu mornings in all phases (3×/week).
- Phase 1: 20–35 min low–moderate (RPE 3–4)
- Phase 2: 25–35 min low–moderate; one fed tempo permissible on week 8.
- Phase 3: 30–35 min low–moderate fasted only; avoid HIIT fasted.
- Monitor glucose pre and 30 min post until patterns stable.

Cheat meal rules (once/week)
- One meal per week (Friday dinner recommended) — one meal only, moderate portion.
- Keep portion sensible (approx. 600–900 kcal depending on weekly budget), avoid bingeing, and do not make it a whole-day event.
- Best placed after resistance training (post‑exercise) to blunt postprandial spikes.
- If alcohol included: limit to 1–2 standard drinks; monitor overnight glucose.

Intermittent fasting (IF) guidance rolled in
- Default TRE: 12:12 eating window (07:30–19:30) so she can have post‑fasted cardio breakfast and still support later resistance work.
- If she prefers to trial 16:8 do so cautiously and only with monitoring; ensure all HIIT and heavy lifts are inside the eating window or with a pre‑workout snack.
- Keep protein spread across meals inside the window to meet daily target.

Sample daily timing (example Monday)
- 06:15 — Fasted AM walk 30 min (RPE 3–4). Pre‑session glucose checked; if <5.0 mmol/L eat 10–15 g carbs.
- 07:30 — Breakfast (post‑cardio): 2 eggs scrambled + spinach + 1 slice wholegrain toast + small fruit (30–40 g carbs, 20–25 g protein).
- 12:30 — Lunch: grilled chicken salad + quinoa 1/2 cup cooked + olive oil dressing (30–40 g carbs, 30 g protein).
- 15:30 — Snack pre‑resistance: Greek yogurt + 1 small banana (20–25 g carbs, 15–20 g protein).
- 17:30 — Resistance session.
- 18:30 — Post‑workout snack/meal: protein shake + small sandwich or balanced dinner (20–30 g carbs + 20–30 g protein).
- 20:30 — End of eating window.

Monitoring and reassessment
- Log weights and waist weekly; training loads and reps each session.
- Glucose: daily fasting morning checks first 2 weeks; pre and 30–60 min post new session types or higher intensity weeks. Log cheat meal responses (pre and 1‑hour post).
- Reassess at 4 weeks and 8 weeks; adjust calories and/or increase protein if needed. Expect potential HbA1c improvements over 3 months; coordinate recheck with GP.

Recovery & lifestyle
- Sleep 7–9 hours nightly.
- Daily NEAT encouraged (extra walking) and standing breaks.
- Stress management: breathing, short walks, mobility.
- Reduce alcohol, especially on heavy training days.

Coaching tips and red flags
- If client reports recurrent hypoglycaemia, dizziness, or syncopal episodes, stop escalating and seek immediate medical review.
- If persistent fatigue, poor sleep, loss of appetite, or mood changes occur during Phase 3, scale back intensity.
- Maintain communication with her GP if weight changes are large or if medication adjustments are considered.
